explanation: N340+ fires on tokens from the vocabulary of grave wrongdoing against people and the institutions that punish it: murder, rape, molestation, torture, genocide, massacre, lynching, kidnapping, assassination, terrorist, unlawful, contraband; the enforcement and sanction lexicon (criminal, police, FBI, surveillance, investigation, arrest, custody, prosecution, warrant, jail, prison, imprisonment, conviction, penalties); oppression, corruption and abuse (censorship, persecution, discrimination, oppressive, corruption, fraud, beaten, harassed, humiliated, expelled) and verbal abuse or profanity (insult, disrespect, bastard, bitch, troll). It is a retrospective lexical detector whose peak sits on the token carrying the loaded word (usually its final subword piece, with surrounding context able to add roughly half again the strength) and which stays at exactly zero for positive or neutral text, ordinary misfortune and illness (cancer, flood, injury, bankruptcy, poverty), negative emotion (fear, grief, anger, shame), property crime (theft, robbery, burglary, shoplifting) and legal boilerplate (contract, clause, license, liability, statute); the one systematic trigger outside this vocabulary is the Japanese causative auxiliary させ, which I cannot yet account for.
